finding.claim: A key of '' or null disables signature verification in createVerifier, so an unsigned token whose alg is in the allowlist is accepted (fail-open). Severity high if the deployment hits it; likelihood depends on config.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled token: unsigned b64url(header).b64url(payload). with alg in the configured algorithms allowlist. Precondition: server passes key '' or null (e.g. unset env var defaulting to '' or '?? null') and sets a non-empty algorithms option.
finding.sink: Signature verification at src/verifier.js:169 is skipped (signature falsy), so the protected operation (authentication) passes without a key.

trace.note: keyType check accepts 'string' and 'object', so '' and null pass validation
'if (key && keyType !== function)' is false for '' and null, so prepareKeyOrSecret (empty-key guard at line 38-40) never runs and key stays ''/null
BASE64URL_RE is /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]*$/, which accepts an empty signature segment
hasKey is false for ''/null
'!hasKey && signature' is false because signature is '' so no missingKey error
token alg is checked against allowedAlgorithms, which passes for an allowlisted alg
signature check skipped because signature is falsy
attacker-chosen payload returned as verified

The async key path is not affected (empty key rejected at line 464). Without the algorithms option, allowedAlgorithms is [] and the token is rejected. finding.claim: Cache entries for tokens without an iat claim use cacheTTL as their max lifetime and ignore exp, so an expired token is accepted from cache for up to cacheTTL (default 10 min) after its exp.
finding.source: A previously issued, legitimately signed token that has exp but no iat (issuer uses noTimestamp: true, or a third-party token lacks iat). Precondition: the cache option is enabled (off by default).
finding.sink: Cache-hit path returns a successful verification after exp (src/verifier.js:377), a protected expiry check.

trace.note: first verification succeeds (exp in future); cacheSet called

cacheValue[2] stays 0 so max = clockTimestamp + clockTolerance + cacheTTL (default 600000 from line 499)
later call after exp: cache lookup returns the entry
min === 0 and now <= max both hold, so cache hit
handleCachedResult returns the expired token's payload as valid

finding.guards_checked: Cache is opt-in: createCache returns null when cache is undefined (src/verifier.js:83-86). The first verification does check exp (src/verifier.js:319). The window is bounded by cacheTTL, about 10 minutes by default. Not executed; verified by reading.

finding.claim: Non-canonical base64url signature encodings are accepted, so one token has multiple valid string forms (malleability), despite a comment saying non-canonical encodings are rejected.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled signature segment of an otherwise valid token, where the final character's unused trailing bits are varied.
finding.sink: Signature bytes decoded by Buffer.from(signature,'base64') at src/crypto.js:339 and compared at src/crypto.js:343; the token string itself is the protected identity used by any application-level replay or revocation store.

trace.note: BASE64URL_RE checks only the alphabet, not canonical length or trailing bits
comment claims non-canonical encodings are rejected, which the code does not do
signature segment accepted with any trailing-bit variant
base64 decode ignores the unused trailing bits, so different strings yield the same signature bytes
